questions.questionText:
Each of the factors of production earns an income.
What are the incomes for land and capital?
land capital

options.text: rent interest
rent profit
wages interest
wages profit

questions.questionText:
A firm decides to stop manufacturing ovens and to produce washing machines instead.
What is the opportunity cost to the firm?

options.text: the additional washing machines produced
the cost of producing ovens
the cost of producing washing machines
the loss of the production of ovens

questions.questionText: What is an advantage of the market economic system?

options.text: It aims for equality of income.
It ensures the provision of defence and law and order.
It gives an incentive to produce.
It reduces pollution and congestion.

questions.questionText: What is meant by the economic problem?

options.text: how to achieve efficiency with the existence of fixed resources and limited wants
how to allocate resources between public and private sectors
how to balance unlimited wants against finite resources
how to decide which methods to use to exploit all resources

questions.questionText:
The table shows the changes in two influences on the demand for and supply of televisions.
If these two changes occurred at the same time, in which case is it impossible for the price of
televisions to rise?
consumers’ incomes costs of production

options.text: fall fall
fall rise
rise fall
rise rise

questions.questionText:
In a country where the demand for petrol (gas) is price-inelastic, the incidence of any increase in
petrol tax will be mainly on

options.text: the company that refines the oil.
the motorist who buys the petrol.
the petrol station that sells the petrol.
the wholesale company that stores the petrol.

questions.questionText: What is an example of market failure?

options.text: a growth of competition
an existence of scarcity
a spread of pollution
a surplus of production in the short-term

questions.questionText: Which action by the operators of an airport directly reduces external costs?

options.text: the stopping of night flights
the building of a new runway
the payment of a productivity bonus
the reduction of charges for landing aircraft

questions.questionText:
A person wishes to buy shares in order to make a long-term profit, but wants as little risk of
short-term loss as possible.
Which type of share is most likely to meet these wishes?

options.text: a share in a coffee growing company
a share in a fashion house
a share in a high-tech electronics company
a share in a supermarket chain

questions.questionText: Which statement about a country’s banks is correct?

options.text: Commercial banks hold the financial accounts of the government.
Commercial banks settle debts by clearing customers’ cheques.
The central bank sets the government’s tax and spending policies.
The central bank supplies foreign currency to members of the public.

questions.questionText: Why might factory workers have higher wage rates than agricultural workers?

options.text: Factory workers are in greater supply.
Factory workers face fewer risks of accidents.
Factory workers have cleaner working conditions.
Factory workers use more productive equipment.

questions.questionText:
A musician has a choice of playing for an orchestra in either England or Germany.
Which combination of incomes and cost of living is most likely to cause her to choose the
German orchestra?
Incomes and cost of living in Germany compared with those in England
pre-tax (gross) income after-tax (net) income cost of living

options.text: higher higher higher
higher lower lower
lower higher higher
lower higher lower

questions.questionText: What may cause an individual to save a higher proportion of their income?

options.text: a belief that the price of goods will rise in the future
a fall in the rate of interest paid by the country’s banks
a fear that income will fall in the future
a rise in the individual’s wish to enjoy higher consumption immediately

questions.questionText: Which change must occur when a firm starts to experience diseconomies of scale?

options.text: Average costs begin to rise.
Employees are made redundant.
Profits turn into losses.
Variable costs become fixed.

questions.questionText: If a firm increases its output in the short run, what will happen to its average fixed cost (AFC)?

options.text: AFC will decrease continually.
AFC will equal zero.
AFC will increase then decrease.
AFC will increase continually.

questions.questionText:
Cathay Pacific, Hong Kong’s largest airline, flies to a number of countries.
Shares in the firm are owned by both individuals and other firms in a number of countries. The
shares are traded on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.
Which type of business organisation is Cathay Pacific?

options.text: a partnership
a private limited company
a public corporation
a public limited company

questions.questionText:
A major computer company announced that its profits had fallen below the level predicted.
What might have caused this?

options.text: increased advertising costs that greatly improved sales
low prices that made the company’s product competitive
new technology that reduced costs
reduced sales and low prices

questions.questionText: When is a direct tax described as progressive?

options.text: when the government changes the basic rate of tax in each budget
when the government taxes companies rather than individuals
when the tax takes a larger proportion of earnings as earnings increase
when the tax takes a smaller proportion of earnings as earnings increase

questions.questionText:
In 2008, the government of Argentina imposed a tax on exports of wheat and soya beans.
What was the most likely aim of this tax?

options.text: to increase agricultural output
to increase exports
to reduce a budget surplus
to reduce the rise in domestic food prices

questions.questionText:
During 2009 some governments adopted policies to try to end the recession in their country and
increase economic growth.
Which combination of policies is most likely to achieve this?

options.text: lower taxes and decrease government spending
lower taxes and increase government spending
raise taxes and decrease government spending
raise taxes and increase government spending

questions.questionText:
The central bank of Mexico set its rate of interest to try to keep the rise in the price level to
only 3%.
Which government aim was it directly trying to achieve?

options.text: balance of payments equilibrium
economic growth
full employment
low inflation

questions.questionText: Why may GDP not be a good measure to compare the standard of living of two countries?

options.text: It does not include government expenditure.
It does not take account of population size.
It is based on a sample ‘basket of goods’.
It only compares export prices with import prices.

questions.questionText:
The table shows the percentage change in employment over a period for a country with three
economic sectors.
percentage (%) change
economic sector
in employment
agriculture –6
manufacturing +2
services +4
Which statement must be correct?

options.text: Agricultural output fell.
The country became more developed.
The working population stayed constant.
Total employment remained the same.

questions.questionText:
Many developed countries are faced with an ageing population.
What is the likely result of this?

options.text: a reduced dependency ratio
increased mobility of labour
increased spending on medical care
reduced tax levels

questions.questionText:
The table shows statistics for four countries in southern Africa.
From the information given, which country has the lowest standard of living?
average annual population density real GDP
life
growth rate of per square per capita
expectancy
population (%) kilometre (US$)
What is likely to happen as a developing country becomes more developed?

options.text: A higher percentage of children will attend school.
Infant mortality will rise.
Life expectancy will fall.
The agricultural sector will increase in importance.

questions.questionText:
A government may use customs barriers to restrict free trade.
What is an economic reason for doing this?

options.text: to discourage the production of strategic goods
to improve the balance of trade
to increase a balance of payments deficit
to make imports cheaper

questions.questionText:
The diagrams show the composition of exports and imports of a country.
Exports Imports
goods services goods services
50% 50% 60% 40%
total exports $120million total imports $100million
What is true for this country?

options.text: There was a deficit in the balance of trade in goods.
There was a deficit in the balance of trade in services.
There was a surplus in the balance of trade in goods.

There was a surplus in the balance of trade in services.
